name: $k$-Block Littlestone Dimension ($k\ge2$)
definition: Fix $k\ge2$. A **$k$-block Littlestone tree** of depth $d$ has a domain-point label $x_v$ at every node $v\in\{0,1\}^{<d}$ and is shattered in the ordinary Littlestone sense. In each block beginning at level $qk$, the root label may be arbitrary, while for every $1\le r<k$ all nodes at level $qk+r$ below the same block root have one common label. Thus a block fixes $k$ coordinates before their joint label in $\{0,1\}^k$ is revealed, and has $2^k$ outcomes. $\mathrm{B}_k(\mathcal{H})$ is the largest total number $d$ of queried coordinates in a shattered $k$-block tree.
graph_summary: Maximum total query depth of a shattered tree with non-adaptive batches of $k$ coordinates.
description: Database-defined structural variant; no published origin is claimed. Although the raw depths $\mathrm B_k$ are not ordered across $k$, the number of complete blocks $\lfloor\mathrm B_k/k\rfloor$ is non-increasing in $k$.

monotonic.proof: A constrained shattered tree for a subfamily is still shattered by every containing class, with exactly the same block-label constraints.

p_monotonic.proof: Every coordinate queried by a shattered tree for a projection is retained.  Lift, for each leaf, a projected realizing hypothesis to an original hypothesis; the same tree is then shattered before projection and retains its block constraints.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, so it cannot create a larger constrained shattered tree.
